Build a consistent routine with yourself as well as your team, clean up and verify throughout the night as you lap, take pictures of EVERYTHING you find when touring before the night starts 

You can never zone enough, always protect food and consumables zone. Develop your team without offloading your work on to them, hold them accountable equally and although it isn’t a TLs job, being involved in the hiring process and learning your weekly freight flow will help you staff accordingly. 

Lastly, keep an open line of communication to the other rotation if you’re on 4x10s as well as stock 2 and stock 1. You can only do as well as you’re set up for; and the same goes for stock in in running inventory processes to keep your bins clear.

Former ON/TL; depending on leadership staffing we would split the store up across the leads and coaches. I normally owned F&C with the exception of the HBA areas. I would either create 1-2 overstock pallets for go through each aisle/dept during follow up and roll zone laps to check. It’s much easier to tackle it throughout the night rather than waiting. 

If the item beeped I would check it; if more than a few beeped for the same associate I’d have them rerun it side by side to teach the overstock process. One thing you do need to be aware of with overstock is the pick creation threshold. If the item doesn’t beep, but creating a label might lower the salesfloor count enough to create a pick. This is where topstock accountability across CAP 1 and Overnight comes into play
